tb21_profile.skill: Implement a chosen-plaintext differential attack on a Feistel cipher: read the round function, pick an input difference whose characteristic survives to the last round, query the encryption oracle on pairs, and score/eliminate candidate round keys - all inside a 30-second budget over a keyspace too big to brute force outright.
tb21_profile.domain: Symmetric cryptography: FEAL, Feistel networks, XOR differentials, round-key schedules, Python bit twiddling on uint32 words.
tb21_profile.task_form: Implement-a-published-attack-from-spec against a given oracle, with a hard wall-clock budget and a single returned value.

notes: CalibForge's `mathematics` category is a purpose-built cryptanalysis suite whose instructions match this TB2.1 task almost word for word ('The file /app/X.py implements ... Implement an attack in /app/attack.py with a function attack(...)'), and it is the only corpus with real block-cipher cryptanalysis. But a whole-corpus grep found only three such tasks, and two of them - mathematics_20260606_172622_001 (4-round Feistel round-key recovery, the single best instruction match anywhere in the pool) and mathematics_20260514_011125_001 (Heys SPN linear cryptanalysis) - are FREE in the packet, so under the hard rule my final list loses them. That is the biggest single cost the FREE rule imposes across my five tasks; verifier_strength.json now grades both `strong`, so the merge step should re-check and promote mathematics_20260606_172622_001 if it trusts that file. With those excluded, the honest final list is 6 TMax + 3 CalibForge + 1 TerminalWorld. TMax has ~99 cryptanalysis hits and its LCG/known-plaintext/weak-block-cipher tasks transfer well even though none says 'differential'; retrieval buried them under generic incident-response XOR-decryption chores. Terminal-Lego has no cryptanalysis at all beyond task_13960 (XOR) - the rest of its list is keyspace/bit-manipulation transfer and caps at overall 3-4. Recursive-Task-Synthesis only implements crypto or reverses crackmes and is `absent` throughout. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench are both weak: their only real contributions are paramiko's KDF, oauthlib signature verification, cantools CRC/SecOC, and borg's buzhash XOR-seed cancellation, which is the one entry there with genuine differential-style reasoning.
